name: WHO emergencies
summary: WHO's Bundibugyo Ebola emergency of international concern remains in force; no new PHEIC found to 10 Nov
state: WHO declared the Bundibugyo Ebola epidemic a public health emergency of international concern on 17 May, and UKHSA's report for the week ending 1 Nov notes it stayed one after the Emergency Committee met on 18 Aug. ECDC's 6 Nov update shows transmission continuing in DR Congo. Searches to 10 Nov found no new PHEIC declared in the past 30 days and no further Emergency Committee meeting announced, so the level stays Watch.
for_you: An emergency is in force for Ebola in central Africa. Travellers should check FCDO travel advice and NHS fit-for-travel guidance before visiting affected areas.
rubric_hit: A PHEIC (Bundibugyo Ebola, declared 17 May) in effect; none new in past 30 days

why: A WHO Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) or 'pandemic emergency' is the top official global health alarm.
drivers: Outbreak spread, IHR Emergency Committee decisions.

rubric.alert: A new PHEIC declared in the past 30 days, or a pandemic emergency declared.
rubric.watch: A PHEIC in effect, or an IHR Emergency Committee convened.
rubric.normal: No PHEIC in effect other than long-running polio.
